title: MEDTRUM Nano disconnecting
body:
After updating with https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/pull/3270, 
is the pump unreachable after an accidental disconnection (long phone distance) and no longer available.
--------------
Before the update, the phone (watch with full android) worked normally with the pump. 
I have been using it in this combination since 20.09.2023.
- 3.3.0-dev-b-app-full-release
- pump model - MD8201, FW 1.80.83
- phone model - KOSPET Optimus2, Android 10.7- non-standard, but fully functional until the last update.

To reconnect the pump, you must exit and restart the application. Then the pump will connect correctly. 

![image](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/assets/54218454/97571057-c904-447d-be75-52606c4f158a)
[Log Export (1).txt](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/files/14771939/Log.Export.1.txt)

comments.body:
Interesting device..
How are other Bluetooth devices working? Other pumps, dash etc?

Before I make any modifications to the code, can you double check the following:
- Location permission set to "always allow"
- ANY powersaving measures for app, Bluetooth app. and general ?

Also can you send me logs which also contains successful connection ?

I've been using different types of watches, customized with Nova Launcher, since 2020, the problem still remains battery life. So far I have only used it in combination with the DANA R and MEDTRUM Nano and the connection works quite correctly. Sometimes it happens that the signal from the Dexcom drops out, but it comes back on after a few minutes. The devices connected via Bluetooth are only the Dexcom G6 transmitter and pump, nothing else.  

All settings are correct, I have enabled constant location access, Bluetooth enabled in the app. I don't have the battery saver activated. Before the modification it worked correctly and when I install the older version, the pump disconnection does not happen.

Log attached. 
[Log Export-succesful.txt](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/files/14785475/Log.Export-succesful.txt)

I reinstalled with an older version and the fact that the connection works properly can be seen from the editing of the basals and smb, see picture. 
![image](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/assets/54218454/ab66b08c-ad6b-4292-ab81-911332b2220f)

It looks your device needs to scan to properly wake up or reset the Bleutooth when a connection attempt fails.
However other devices don't handle scanning on every connection error too well. (see: https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/issues/3268)

I see few options

1. Add a retry mechanism and after 3 retries we start scanning anyway
2. Add a setting, for those phones who need it can enable scanning.
3. Add a check if android version is < 11 and do scanning for those devices. (This is a bit tricky as we only have 1 complaint so far with the new code)

@MilosKozak any thoughts ?

@jbr7rr it's up to you
if there is only one device affected i'd add option available in eng mode only
